title: The Decomposition Is the Fingerprint: Per-Component Identity for Agent Skills
title_zh: 分解即指纹：面向智能体技能的逐组件身份识别
abstract_en: AI agents increasingly acquire and execute skills at runtime: bundles of prompt instructions, executable code, and tool declarations fetched from marketplaces and other agents. Governing them needs a stable notion of skill identity, yet cryptographic hashing is engineered to destroy the very similarity we need, as a one-character edit scrambles the digest. We present a compact, locality-sensitive fingerprint that embeds each component of a skill and projects it to bits with a multi-bank SimHash, giving a fixed 120-byte signature compared in constant time by Hamming distance. Our central claim is that keeping the fingerprint as a per-component triple (prompt, code, tools), rather than a single score, is what makes it useful: the triple recovers skill-family identity through paraphrase, renaming, refactoring, and controlled code translation when another component remains shared, while independent multilingual reimplementation is not recovered; it also localizes which component carries the reuse. We claim lineage, not behavioral equivalence: identity supplies the structural axis of a registry and leaves safety to behavioral verification. The fingerprint reaches an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.974 (95% CI [0.956, 0.994]) over 4,950 pairwise comparisons while using 77x fewer bits than the embedding it approximates, with ranking preserved in expectation and finite-bit concentration; the per-component split turns one number into relationship classification, families, novelty, and a portable "SkillBOM" for a skill registry. On a 906-skill injection benchmark the fingerprint recognizes injected skills as tampered copies of a known base and localizes the change, but recognition is not trust: it remains, by design, an identity signal complementary to behavioral verification rather than a safety verdict.
abstract_zh: 本文关注 AI agents 在运行时获取并执行“技能”（包含 prompt 指令、可执行代码和工具声明）时的身份治理问题。传统加密哈希对微小改动极其敏感，无法保留技能之间的相似性。作者提出一种紧凑的局部敏感指纹方法：分别对技能的 prompt、code、tools 三个组件进行嵌入，并通过多组 SimHash 投影为固定 120 字节签名，可用 Hamming distance 常数时间比较。论文核心观点是，保留逐组件三元组指纹比单一相似度更有用：它能在改写、重命名、重构、受控代码翻译等情况下恢复技能家族关系，并定位复用来自哪个组件；但对独立的多语言重实现不会错误地恢复同源关系。该方法强调识别的是 lineage（谱系/结构身份），而非行为等价或安全性。实验显示，该指纹在 4,950 个成对比较上达到 AUC 0.974（95% CI [0.956, 0.994]），相比原嵌入节省 77 倍比特；在 906 个技能注入基准上可识别被篡改的已知技能副本并定位修改，但其结果仅作为身份信号，仍需行为验证补充安全判断。
key_points_zh: 提出面向 AI agent 技能的紧凑局部敏感指纹，将 prompt、code、tools 分别编码为三元组签名，而非合并为单一分数。
采用多组 SimHash 将组件嵌入压缩为固定 120 字节指纹，可通过 Hamming distance 常数时间比较，并保留相似性排序的期望性质。
逐组件分解可区分技能家族、复用来源与新颖性：能处理 paraphrase、renaming、refactoring 和受控代码翻译，但不会把独立多语言重实现误判为同源。
在 4,950 个成对比较上取得 AUC 0.974，相比被近似的 embedding 少用 77 倍比特；在 906-skill injection benchmark 上可识别已知技能的篡改副本并定位变化组件。
论文明确将该指纹定位为 lineage/identity 信号，而非 behavioral equivalence 或安全 verdict；安全性仍需独立的行为验证机制。

llm_assessment.comment: The per-component skill fingerprint is a useful governance primitive for agent skill registries, lineage tracking, and tamper detection.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: 按组件划分的技能指纹是代理技能注册表、谱系追踪和篡改检测中有用的治理原语。
